claims: "Quilt Pro Special" and "Exceed" are Juki series names for this model tier, not ratings (Juki product page).

Juki says the machine "incorporates JUKI's industrial sewing machine technology to produce superior stitch quality" and that its feeding "can handle even the heaviest" projects (Juki product page). No maximum fabric thickness is published.
Juki's brochure claims "Industrial Quality Buttonholes" and says heavy material projects such as hemming denim jeans can be sewn with ease (Juki F series brochure, dated 0904).
"Industrial-grade stitch quality" (dealer copy, Sewing Machines Plus).
"Sturdier motor to help you sew thick fabrics such as denim and multiple quilting layers" (comparison-site claim; no motor rating published).
conflicts: Throat: Juki publishes no throat, needle-to-arm or arm-size figure for this model. Dealers quote 8 in to the right of the needle and one QuiltingBoard owner measured about 7.75 in, so we hold the throat as [verify]. The Juki brochure marks 551 mm and 112 mm around a quilt on the wide table without defining them, and we do not read either as a throat figure.

Price: Juki lists a $2,369 suggested retail price (dealer pricing only) on its product page, while Michaels showed $1,399 and $1,499 on 2026-09-29 and a review site quoted $1,499 as MSRP. These are separate sources and we do not treat any of them as a firm street price.

Warranty: Juki America's general warranty text gives 2 years on motor and electrical parts and 5 years on other parts, with no '90 days adjustments' term. Only dealers state the 90 days, so it is dropped from our spec.

In the box: Juki's page lists 12 presser feet including a quilt foot and calls one foot 'smooth', where our earlier dealer-sourced list had 10 feet and called it 'Teflon'. We use Juki's names and count.
Stitch count: one Sewing Machines Plus snippet says 255 stitches; Juki and every other dealer say 225. Treated as a typo.
Motor: Juki publishes no motor type, wattage or rating in the page, brochure or manual, so the motor stays [verify].

ownerThemes.theme: Multi-year owners on QuiltingBoard still recommend it for piecing, applique and decorative binding stitches; the recurring caveat is that the harp is not large for heavy free motion quilting.
An owner measured about 7.75 in of throat to the right of the needle, a quarter inch under the dealer figure.
Owners describe it as quiet and easy to use, handling knits and a denim-over-cotton stack without tension trouble; one had a unit go back to the vendor for adjustment.
Setting it into a cabinet is awkward because the bottom row of buttons and the power cord sit low on the front; free motion setup questions come up on PatternReview.

Quilters who want more speed and a straight stitch only compare the 1,500 spm TL at a similar price.
The other mid-price computerized quilting machine, with a 10 in arm against the F600's 8 in.

editorial.verdict: A box-feed computerized HZL with 225 stitches, 900 spm, walking foot, wide table and knee lift listed in the box; Juki publishes no throat figure.
editorial.whoFor: A quilter or garment sewer who wants one computerized machine with the accessories included and can accept an unverified, standard-size arm.
editorial.skipIf: You quilt large tops and need a published 10 in or longer arm, or you only sew straight and would rather have the 1,500 spm TL series.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Juki HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Owners mostly praise how quiet it runs, how it feeds knits and heavier fabric, the threading, the workspace and the lights. The repeated complaints are reliability reports such as timing, bobbin case and tension problems, and oiling and maintenance, which draw more criticism than praise. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the price of the Juki HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Juki's suggested retail price is $2,369, and Juki tells buyers to ask a dealer for pricing. Michaels showed $1,399 on 2026-09-29, and a second Michaels listing showed $1,499 the same day. Dealers set their own prices, so compare dated listings and what is included.

faqs.q: What are the features of the Juki HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Juki lists 225 stitches including 16 sensor buttonholes and 4 lettering fonts, a 900 spm top speed and a box feed with a 7-point feed dog. It trims thread by button, programmed trim or the heel of the foot controller, and the brochure lists dual LED lights. Juki's page lists 12 presser feet, a wide table, a hard case and a knee lift lever as standard.

faqs.q: How heavy is the Juki HZL-F600?
faqs.a: 21.6 lb (9.8 kg) per Juki's page, brochure and manual, the same as the F300 and F400. Juki's page gives 17.5 in wide, 11.5 in high and 8.25 in deep.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki HZL-F300 and HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Per Juki pages and brochure: 225 stitches and 4 fonts against 106 and 3, two LED lights against one, random stitches on the F600 only, and the wide table and knee lever standard on the F600 but optional on the F300. Speed, needle, weight and size are identical. Juki lists $2,369 against $1,799.

faqs.q: How big is the throat on the Juki HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Juki does not publish one. Dealers quote 8 in to the right of the needle and one QuiltingBoard owner measured about 7.75 in, so we show it as [verify]. Juki's brochure marks 551 mm and 112 mm on a wide-table picture without defining them.

faqs.q: Does the Juki HZL-F600 come with a walking foot and extension table?
faqs.a: Yes per Juki's page: 12 presser feet including a walking foot and a quilt foot, a wide table, a hard case and a knee lift lever. Juki calls one foot 'smooth'; some dealers call it Teflon.

faqs.q: Can the Juki HZL-F600 sew denim and thick layers?
faqs.a: Owners report denim aprons, four layers of denim and multi-layer quilting cotton, and one says a very thick seam may need hand walking. Juki's brochure claims heavy projects like denim hems sew with ease, and Juki publishes no motor rating or maximum thickness.

faqs.q: What needles and bobbins does the Juki HZL-F600 use?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists 130R / 705H needles with a low shank and a class 15 drop-in bobbin. The box holds 4 bobbins.
